conclusions: Knott hired them to clear the house's name; research before entry is wise but not mandatory.
Walter Corbitt's body was interred in the house basement per his will; his mind still haunts from there.
Central Library records establish the house's construction, Corbitt's long and hostile tenure, and the unresolved litigation over his burial.
Corbitt preserved his identity with Mythos magic and can animate his corpse; he is not a harmless shade.
The Corbitt House's tragedies are caused by Corbitt's lingering will — not mere bad luck or a conventional ghost story.
Corbitt's own ritual dagger bypasses his spells and can reduce him to ash.
